full_text_en:
**Shanghai Ansheng Property Co., Ltd. v. Wang Wenzheng — labor contract dispute**

**[Case Gist]**

An employer’s exercise of management authority shall be reasonable and in good faith. Where an employee submits leave procedures due to a critical illness of a direct family member, and during the employer’s approval process, that direct family member passes away, and the employee directly returns home to handle the funeral, the employer’s subsequent termination of the labor contract on the ground of absenteeism constitutes an illegal termination of the labor contract and is also inconsistent with social ethics. Where the employee claims compensation due to the employer’s illegal termination of the labor contract, the people's court shall support such claim.

**Plaintiff:** Shanghai Ansheng Property Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Shanghai Hu Qing Ping Highway.

**Legal Representative:** Mei Yuejing, Executive Director of the company.

**Defendant:** Wang Wenzheng, male, born on September 18, 1969, Han ethnicity, domiciled in Jing County, Anhui Province.

The plaintiff, Shanghai Ansheng Property Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Ansheng Company), filed a lawsuit with the Qingpu District People’s Court of Shanghai against the defendant, Wang Wenzheng, due to a labor contract dispute.

**Plaintiff’s Allegations:** The plaintiff, Ansheng Company, established a labor relationship with the defendant Wang Wenzheng from April 7, 2008. Wang Wenzheng worked as a security guard for Ansheng Company. On the morning of January 6, 2020, Wang Wenzheng, citing his father’s critical illness, requested temporary personal leave from January 6 to 13. He submitted the leave application form to the security team leader Li, asking Li to forward it, and stated that he would contact the community manager Wu himself. He then took a bus back to his hometown. At noon that day, Wang Wenzheng notified the property management office of this leave matter by phone. Wu took a photo of the leave form and uploaded it to the company’s WeChat group, but approval was not obtained. After learning that the leave was not approved, Wang Wenzheng was originally on his way back to the unit on January 7, but on the way he received a call about his father’s death and returned to his hometown. He returned to Shanghai on the afternoon of January 14 and started work on the 15th. The company’s attendance and other rules and regulations were lawfully formulated, publicized to Wang Wenzheng, and he was organized to study them. Wang Wenzheng signed to confirm, knew them, and should strictly comply. According to the company’s attendance management rules, an employee applying for personal leave for three consecutive days or more (including three days) requires approval by the group company’s president (general manager). Anyone who accumulates absenteeism for three days or more (including three days) is deemed to have seriously violated the company’s rules and regulations and labor discipline. The company has the right to dismiss, terminate the labor contract early, and not pay economic compensation according to law. During the period from January 6 to 14, 2020, Wang Wenzheng took leave without approval, totaling 6 working days of absence. Even if three days of bereavement leave are granted, the cumulative absenteeism still reaches three working days, meeting the conditions for dismissal. Ansheng Company disagrees with the arbitration award. Human feelings cannot override the law; the legitimate rights and interests of the employer also need to be protected. Wang Wenzheng, knowing the company’s attendance approval system and that this personal leave was not approved according to regulations either in advance or afterwards, still intentionally absented himself. The circumstances have reached the standard for dismissal. Therefore, Ansheng Company’s termination of the labor contract is lawful, does not constitute illegal termination, and no compensation is required. Wang Wenzheng’s 2019 annual leave has been fully used, so Ansheng Company does not need to pay the wage difference for unused annual leave. Therefore, Ansheng Company requests that the court rule: Ansheng Company shall not pay Wang Wenzheng compensation for illegal termination of labor contract in the amount of RMB 75,269.04, nor the wage difference for unused annual leave in 2019 in the amount of RMB 856.1.

**Defendant’s Defense:** The defendant disagrees with the plaintiff Ansheng Company’s claims and accepts the arbitration award.

**Facts Found by the Court at First Instance (Qingpu District People’s Court of Shanghai):**

The defendant Wang Wenzheng started working for the plaintiff Ansheng Company on April 7, 2008, as a security guard, with a work schedule of two days on and one day off. Employees of Ansheng Company applying for personal leave or public leave must fill in a leave application form, specifying the type of leave, time, reason, etc. The signature columns at the bottom of the form are “Applicant,” “Duty Agent,” “Supervising Department,” “Department Head,” “Personnel,” and “Manager.” Ansheng Company’s attendance management rules stipulate that an employee’s one-day personal leave requires approval by the supervisor, two consecutive days require approval by the Administrative Affairs Department (Office), and three consecutive days or more (including three days) require approval by the company’s president (general manager); cumulative absenteeism of three days or more (including three days) is deemed a serious violation of the company’s rules and labor discipline, and the company has the right to dismiss, terminate the labor contract early, and not pay economic compensation according to law. Wang Wenzheng signed to confirm that he had studied the above documents. On January 6, 2020, Wang Wenzheng, because his father was ill, submitted a leave form to his supervisor Li and then returned to his hometown. The leave period was from January 6 to 13, 2020. The next day, Wang Wenzheng returned because Ansheng Company did not approve the leave. On the way, he learned of his father’s death and went back home again to handle the funeral. Afterwards, Wang Wenzheng returned to Shanghai on January 14, 2020, and started work the next day. During the period from January 6 to 14, 2020, Wang Wenzheng’s scheduled working days were January 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, and 14, totaling 6 days. On January 31, 2020, Ansheng Company issued a “Notice of Termination of Labor Contract” to Wang Wenzheng, terminating the labor relationship on the ground that the cumulative absenteeism days reached three days or more (including three days).

It was further found that Wang Wenzheng was entitled to 10 days of annual leave in 2019, of which he had taken 7 days. During the period from August 1, 2019 to July 31, 2020, the security guard position of the plaintiff Ansheng Company implemented a comprehensive working hour system calculated on a quarterly cycle.

It was also found that the defendant Wang Wenzheng applied for arbitration on March 27, 2020, requesting the plaintiff Ansheng Company to pay wages for January and February 2020 in the amount of RMB 11,190.53, compensation for illegal termination of the labor contract in the amount of RMB 104,069.06, and the wage difference for unused annual leave in 2019 in the amount of RMB 2,464.38. The arbitration award ruled that Ansheng Company should pay Wang Wenzheng wages for January 2020 of RMB 3,419.3, compensation for illegal termination of the labor contract of RMB 75,269.04, and the wage difference for unused annual leave in 2019 of RMB 865.16, and dismissed Wang Wenzheng’s other claims. Ansheng Company, dissatisfied with the award, filed this lawsuit with the court.

During the trial, the defendant Wang Wenzheng provided the court with: 1. A certificate issued by the village committee, proving that his father died of illness on January 7, 2020, and was cremated on January 12. The death certificate was given to the funeral home, and the cremation certificate was given to the public security authorities when canceling the household registration, so there are currently no death certificate or cremation certificate. The plaintiff Ansheng Company did not acknowledge the authenticity, arguing that the death certificate should be issued by the public security bureau and the cremation certificate by the funeral home. Even if the village committee certificate is genuine, it is inconsistent with common sense for Wang Wenzheng’s father to have died on January 7 and been cremated on January 12. 2. WeChat chat records between Wang Wenzheng and the security team leader Li, in which Li said at approximately 9:57 p.m. on January 7, 2020, “Rest assured and handle your old father’s funeral. I will communicate with Manager Wu and higher-ups tomorrow.” This was to prove that his leave was approved by his supervisor. Ansheng Company had no objection to the authenticity but argued that this evidence exactly proves that Wang Wenzheng knew that the leave was not approved, and Li clearly stated that he did not have the authority to approve.

**Reasoning of the First Instance Court (Qingpu District People’s Court of Shanghai):**

An employer’s exercise of management authority shall follow the principles of reasonableness, limits, and good faith. Termination of a labor contract is the most severe disciplinary sanction, and the employer shall use it prudently. The defendant Wang Wenzheng’s return to his hometown to handle his father’s funeral was not only dealing with an urgent family matter but also fulfilling his filial piety as a son, which is in line with the traditional human ethics and good customs of the Chinese nation. The plaintiff Ansheng Company, as the employer, should give full respect, understanding, and tolerance. Wang Wenzheng provided a certificate issued by the village committee. Although Ansheng Company did not accept it, it provided no contrary evidence to overturn it. The nature of the personal leave requested by Wang Wenzheng from January 6 to 13 changed after January 7, becoming a combination of personal leave and bereavement leave. Deducting three days of bereavement leave, Wang Wenzheng actually only requested two days of personal leave. Considering that Wang Wenzheng’s hometown is in another province and the travel time is considerable, Wang Wenzheng’s request for two days of personal leave was within a reasonable period. Ansheng Company’s refusal to approve was obviously inconsiderate and also contrary to the purpose of establishing the personal leave system. Ansheng Company’s termination of the labor contract, without regard for the background and reasons of the event, mechanically applying the rules and regulations, and strictly implementing employment management, was clearly inappropriate. Therefore, Ansheng Company shall pay Wang Wenzheng compensation for illegal termination of the labor contract in the amount of RMB 75,269.04. Regarding the wages for annual leave in 2019, Wang Wenzheng had 3 days of unused annual leave. Ansheng Company shall pay Wang Wenzheng the wage difference for unused annual leave in the amount of RMB 865.16. Regarding wages for January 2020, the arbitration award ruled that Ansheng Company should pay Wang Wenzheng wages of RMB 3,419.3 for January 2020. Both parties did not file a lawsuit on this matter, which shall be deemed as acceptance, and the court confirms it.

Accordingly, the Qingpu District People’s Court of Shanghai, in accordance with Article 47, paragraphs 1 and 3, and Article 87 of the *Labor Contract Law of the People’s Republic of China*, and Article 3, paragraph 1, and Article 5, paragraph 3 of the *Regulations on Paid Annual Leave for Employees*, rendered the judgment on October 10, 2020:

I. The plaintiff Shanghai Ansheng Property Co., Ltd. shall pay the defendant Wang Wenzheng compensation for illegal termination of the labor contract in the amount of RMB 75,269.04 within ten days from the date this judgment takes legal effect;

II. The plaintiff Shanghai Ansheng Property Co., Ltd. shall pay the defendant Wang Wenzheng the wage difference for unused annual leave in 2019 in the amount of RMB 865.16 within ten days from the date this judgment takes legal effect;

III. The plaintiff Shanghai Ansheng Property Co., Ltd. shall pay the defendant Wang Wenzheng wages for January 2020 in the amount of RMB 3,419.3 within ten days from the date this judgment takes legal effect.

Ansheng Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People’s Court, arguing: 1. The appellee Wang Wenzheng did not wait for the unit’s approval before taking a bus back to his hometown, indicating that he had unilaterally decided to leave his post and had subjective intent for absenteeism. After Wang Wenzheng left his post, deducting statutory bereavement leave, he had already been absent for 3 days, meeting the conditions for dismissal. The certificate of his father’s death, cremation, and burial provided by Wang Wenzheng was issued by the village committee, and its authenticity cannot be confirmed, so the company has reasonable doubts. 2. Given the special nature of the security guard job, if Wang Wenzheng is not dismissed, other security guards may follow suit, and the company will be unable to effectively manage. For periods exceeding the statutory bereavement leave, the employer has the full right to decide whether to approve or not based on the actual circumstances and work needs. Wang Wenzheng had reached the standard for dismissal, and Ansheng Company made a prudent decision after fully considering the actual circumstances, without violating the principles of reasonableness, limits, and good faith. 3. Wang Wenzheng’s annual leave for 2019 had been fully used, and Ansheng Company is not required to pay the wage difference.

The appellee Wang Wenzheng argued: Wang Wenzheng requested leave because of his father’s death, which was a legitimate reason, and the leave period was within a reasonable range, so it cannot be characterized as absenteeism.

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People’s Court, at second instance, confirmed the facts found at first instance.

**Reasoning of the Second Instance Court (Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People’s Court):**

During the performance of a labor contract, both the employer and the employee have the obligation to perform the contract substantially, fully, and properly. The employee has the duty to consciously maintain the employer’s labor order and comply with the employer’s rules and regulations; the boundaries and manner of exercise of the employer’s management authority shall also be in good faith, tolerant, and reasonable. The appellant Ansheng Company terminated the labor contract between the parties on the ground that the appellee Wang Wenzheng’s cumulative absenteeism days had reached three days or more (including three days). Whether Ansheng Company’s termination was illegal depends on whether Wang Wenzheng had committed the disciplinary violation alleged by the company. Wang Wenzheng’s work schedule was two days on and one day off. During the period from January 6 to 14, 2020, his leave request was from January 6 to 13, and his scheduled working days were January 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, and 14.

First, regarding the period from January 6 to 13. The appellee Wang Wenzheng submitted his leave procedures on the morning of January 6. His supervisors Li and Wu signed their approval. However, his superiors only reported it to the group company for approval in the afternoon and only informed Wang Wenzheng of the disapproval the next day. Therefore, Wang Wenzheng’s absence on January 6 was caused by the appellant Ansheng Company’s failure to timely exercise its approval authority and should not be deemed absenteeism. On January 7, Wang Wenzheng, due to the company’s disapproval of his leave, was on his way back to Shanghai when he learned of his father’s death and went home again to handle the funeral. At this point, the nature of the personal leave changed, becoming a combination of bereavement leave and personal leave. Deducting three days of bereavement leave, Wang Wenzheng’s actual personal leave days were 2 days. As to whether these 2 days of personal leave should have been approved, looking at the whole case, Wang Wenzheng’s request for leave was justified. He returned to his hometown to handle his father’s funeral, which is in line with the traditional human ethics and good customs of the Chinese nation. Ansheng Company, as the employer, should exercise its management authority in accordance with the principles of reasonableness, limits, and good faith. As for Ansheng Company’s doubts about the timing of Wang Wenzheng’s father’s death and cremation/burial, in the vast rural areas of China, including Wang Wenzheng’s hometown in Anhui, there is still a funeral custom of keeping the coffin at home. The time from death to cremation and burial as shown in the relevant village committee certificate is within a reasonable range. Respecting folk customs and showing consideration for employees’ specific difficulties and misfortunes is also part of the employer’s duty. Therefore, Ansheng Company’s argument is not accepted. Secondly, regarding January 14, 2020, this day was not within the scope of Wang Wenzheng’s leave period. Ansheng Company’s classification of this day as absenteeism was not improper.

In summary, the appellee Wang Wenzheng’s absenteeism did not reach three days and did not meet the conditions for termination of the labor contract as stipulated in the appellant Ansheng Company’s rules and regulations. Ansheng Company’s termination was illegal and must pay compensation for illegal termination in the amount of RMB 75,269.04. Regarding the claim for the wage difference for unused annual leave in 2019, the first instance ruling was correct, and the second instance upholds it.

In conclusion, the appellant Ansheng Company’s termination of the labor contract constituted an illegal termination. The first-instance judgment had clear findings of fact, correct application of law, and the ruling was not improper. Accordingly, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People’s Court, in accordance with Article 170, paragraph 1, item (1) of the *Civil Procedure Law of the People’s Republic of China*, rendered the judgment on December 15, 2020:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.
